claims.text: Controlled thermal annealing can enhance chemical short-range order in high-entropy alloy intermediate layers.
Enhanced chemical short-range order will improve lattice thermal conductivity.
Enhanced chemical short-range order will preserve mechanical integrity in plasma-facing applications.
Conventionally sintered high-entropy alloy intermediate layers prioritize structural stability.
Conventionally sintered high-entropy alloy intermediate layers have limited optimized short-range order and lower phonon-based heat transfer.
Optimizing annealing temperature, dwell time, and cooling rate will induce and enhance chemical short-range order.
The proposed effect should hold around 800°C under cyclic mechanical loading.
Enhanced chemical short-range order forms percolated atomic clusters within the alloy matrix.
Chemical short-range order modifies the vibrational or phonon density of states.
Percolating short-range-order clusters create efficient pathways for phonon transport.
The phonon-transport pathways increase lattice thermal conductivity.
Induced short-range order does not detract from the dislocation network or overall mechanical integrity.
The annealed alloy will have approximately 12% or greater thermal-conductivity improvement relative to the unannealed baseline.
The annealed alloy will retain requisite structural strength under plasma-facing operating conditions.
Conventional unannealed high-entropy alloy intermediate layers have robust structural integrity but suboptimal thermal conductivity.
Deviation from approximately 800°C or use of poorly optimized annealing parameters may negate the conductivity benefit or impair structural stability.
In atomistic simulations of HfNbTaTiZr, increasing short-range order produces HfTi and TiZr clusters and raises lattice heat conductivity by around 12%.
